page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.18-72 is a compute-oriented virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor running at a base clock frequency of 3.0 GHz. The system provides 18 dedicated physical cores across an x86_64 architecture, presenting 36 vCPUs via two threads per core. System memory is configured at 72 GB, which establishes a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, operates without hardware GPU accelerators, and does not provide bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent file systems.

Benchmark data reflects balanced processor and memory performance, supported by AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic hardware extensions. Stress-ng scores show 1,944.5 in single-core and 35,764.37 in multi-core metrics. Throughput is notably strong in static web serving benchmarks, recording 44.73 GB/sec in the top 25 percent category. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 156.85 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 70.08 GB/sec for writes. In-memory operations achieve 32.64 million Redis SET operations per second, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 180.99 GB/sec. Machine learning inference runs effectively on small models at 268.66 tokens per second for a 135M architecture, but decreases significantly on larger parameter weights.

The 1:2 compute-to-memory profile prioritizes instruction execution efficiency over expansive RAM allocations. Because local disk volumes are omitted, the server avoids redundant physical storage overhead while relying on remote block storage latency. This balance makes the instance efficient for CPU-bound microservices, high-traffic static web servers, continuous integration build jobs, and batch compression tasks where dedicated core execution prevents noisy-neighbor resource competition.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.18-72 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. Built on an x86_64 architecture, it delivers 18 dedicated physical cores (36 vCPUs) and 72 GB of system memory, adhering to a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or discrete GPUs, relying on external network block storage for persistence. Performance benchmarks highlight robust static web serving throughput at 44.73 GB/sec and capable multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 180.99 GB/sec, alongside average multi-core compute marks in stress-ng evaluations. With dedicated physical core allocation and AVX-512 instruction support, this server configuration provides dependable execution efficiency for parallel continuous integration workloads, high-volume web serving, API gateways, and distributed compute-heavy batch processing.
